svg.title: Real-Time Intelligence Flow: Sources to Eventhouse to Actions
svg.desc: A flow diagram tracing events from external streaming sources into Eventstream, routing to Eventhouse for durable KQL storage and OneLake mirroring, and to Activator for automated actions, governed by Real-Time hub and Outbound Access Protection.
svg.text: Real-Time Intelligence — Ingestion, Storage & Automated Action Flow
Sources ➔ Eventstream Stream Processing ➔ Durable Eventhouse & OneLake Delta ➔ Real-Time Hub & Activator

g.title: Event sources — Kafka, Event Hubs, MQTT, CDC feeds, and other streaming or change-data sources.
g.text: Continuous high-velocity telemetry & database change feeds
• Multi-cloud support: AWS Kinesis, Google Pub/Sub & custom webhooks
Stream securely from on-prem or isolated VNets via Streaming VNet Data Gateways.

g.title: Eventstream — No-code ingestion pipeline: collects, transforms, and routes events to multiple destinations.
g.text: Visual in-flight stream processing, transformation & multi-sink routing
Filter by attribute thresholds in flight
• Derived Eventstreams: Package transformed outputs as reusable tenant streams
• Low-latency pipeline operating with sub-second event forwarding
• Fans out shaped data to multiple destinations simultaneously
1. Eventhouse KQL DB: Durable indexed arrival-time analytics
2. Fabric Activator (Reflex): Real-time alerting & automated action triggers
3. Fabric Lakehouse: Delta format persistence for downstream ELT
4. Custom Endpoints: Azure Event Hubs & External Kafka sinks
✓ Auto-registered into Real-Time Hub for tenant-wide discoverability

svg.text: PHASE 2: DURABLE STORAGE, ONELAKE MIRROR & ACTIONS

g.title: Eventhouse KQL database — Durable, indexed storage organized by arrival time, queryable via KQL or T-SQL.
g.text: Durable high-throughput storage optimized for structured & semi-structured logs
• Records indexed instantly on arrival time — sub-second queries across billions of rows
• Queryable via native Kusto Query Language (KQL) & managed T-SQL endpoint
• KQL Querysets enable interactive exploration, sharing & parameterization
• Hot Cache Tier: In-memory SSD cache for immediate sub-second visual rendering
• Standard Storage: Petabyte-scale cost-effective retention policy management
• Multi-DB Capacity Sharing: Multiple KQL DBs share one underlying compute pool
Built-in series_decompose_anomalies() & geo_distance() evaluate directly in-database.

g.title: OneLake Delta mirror — Eventhouse data mirrors into OneLake as Delta, queryable by every other Fabric engine.
g.text: Zero-ETL data sharing across Power BI Direct Lake, Warehouse, & Spark
• Automatically exposes KQL table data in open Delta Lake Parquet format
• 0 data copying or scheduled pipeline refresh required — 0 additional storage fee
• Adaptive Batching: Accumulates 200–256 MB Parquet files to optimize downstream read
Default delay up to 3h (configurable to 5m). Avoid low delays that produce small file clutter.

g.title: Activator — Watches the stream for threshold, pattern, or KQL-defined conditions and fires actions.
g.text: Continuous rule evaluation & automated action orchestration
Replaces rigid time-based polling schedules with immediate event reaction across tenant.

g.title: Real-Time hub — Organization-wide catalog surfacing every active stream and event source to every workload.
g.text: Centralized directory of streaming data in motion across tenant
• Single discovery surface for all Eventstreams, Azure Events & Fabric Item Events
• Microsoft-Managed CDC: Direct subscription to Azure SQL, Cosmos DB & Postgres
• Fabric Item Events: Job completed, table updated & workspace lifecycle alerts
Teams subscribe directly to existing streams in 2 clicks — 0 duplicate pipelines created
One-click "Set Alert in Activator" or "Open in KQL Queryset" exploration.

g.title: Outbound Access Protection — Cross-workspace event consumption is default-deny unless explicitly allowed.
g.text: Security perimeter governing cross-workspace event consumption
• When OAP is enabled on a workspace, cross-workspace event reading is DEFAULT-DENY
• Eventstream / Activator cannot read Job/OneLake events from another workspace
• Same-workspace event consumption is ALWAYS permitted regardless of OAP state
Requires explicit data connection rule for Real-Time Events connector to unblock.
Paused consumers must be audited within 7-day retention window before events drop.

svg.text: Fabric Atlas — Original Infographic, August 2026. Grounded in Microsoft Fabric Real-Time Intelligence Specs.
